name: Apollo 11
crew: Neil Armstrong, Buzz Aldrin, Michael Collins
summary: First human lunar landing. Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin spent 21.6 hours on the lunar surface at Mare Tranquillitatis.
outcome: Successful first crewed landing; 21.55 kg of lunar samples returned; descent stage and EASEP instruments left on surface.

majorMilestones.title: Launch from Kennedy Space Center LC-39A on Saturn V
Lunar touchdown at Mare Tranquillitatis (Tranquility Base)
First human moonwalk EVA (2 hr 31 min)
Lunar module ascent stage liftoff; descent stage remains
Pacific splashdown and crew recovery

name: Apollo 15
crew: David Scott, James Irwin, Alfred Worden
summary: First 'J-mission' with extended stay (67 hrs) and the debut of the Lunar Roving Vehicle (LRV-001).
outcome: Traversed 27.8 km across Hadley-Apennine, collected the ancient 'Genesis Rock' (4.1 billion years old).

majorMilestones.title: Saturn V launch
Touchdown at Hadley-Apennine
First extraterrestrial drive of the Lunar Roving Vehicle
Ascent liftoff; LRV parked to film liftoff with ground camera

name: Surveyor 1
summary: First American spacecraft to achieve a soft touchdown on another extraterrestrial world.
outcome: Returned 11,237 images demonstrating lunar soil bearing strength sufficient for Apollo astronauts.

majorMilestones.title: Launch aboard Atlas-Centaur
Historic soft touchdown in Oceanus Procellarum
Final telemetry contact following lunar night survival

name: Lunar Orbiter 1
summary: Mapped 5 million square kilometers of lunar surface to select safe Apollo landing sites and took the first Earthrise photo.
outcome: Commanded to impact lunar far side after 577 orbits to clear frequencies for Lunar Orbiter 2.

majorMilestones.title: Launch from Cape Kennedy
First photograph of Earth from the vicinity of the Moon (Earthrise)
Controlled lunar impact on far side

name: Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO)
summary: High-resolution polar mapping orbiter providing 3D global topographic models and imagery of historic landing sites.
outcome: Ongoing active mapping; imaged Apollo landing sites, rover wheel tracks, and confirmed water ice deposits in permanently shadowed craters.

majorMilestones.title: Atlas V launch carrying LRO and LCROSS impactor
Lunar orbit insertion
LROC releases first high-resolution pictures of Apollo landing sites

name: Viking 1
summary: First successful long-duration soft landing on Mars consisting of an Orbiter and Lander.
outcome: Operated for 2,245 sols in Chryse Planitia; delivered first color surface photos, soil chemistry, and atmospheric telemetry.

majorMilestones.title: Titan IIIE launch
Mars orbit insertion
Touchdown at Chryse Planitia
Final transmission after incorrect uplink command

name: Viking 2
summary: Second Viking mission lander deployed to the boulder-strewn plains of Utopia Planitia.
outcome: Recorded 1,281 sols of meteorological, imaging, and biology data.

majorMilestones.title: Titan IIIE launch
Touchdown at Utopia Planitia
Lander battery failure ends communications

name: Mars Pathfinder
summary: Low-cost demonstration of airbag landing technology carrying the first mobile planetary rover, Sojourner.
outcome: Returned 16,500 images and 8.5 million environmental measurements; proved Mars had catastrophic past floods in Ares Vallis.

majorMilestones.title: Delta II launch
Touchdown at Ares Vallis using parachute and airbags
Sojourner rover rolls down ramp onto Martian soil
Final transmission received from lander

name: Mars Exploration Rovers (Spirit & Opportunity)
summary: Twin robotic geologists sent to search for past water activity at Gusev Crater (Spirit) and Meridiani Planum (Opportunity).
outcome: Discovered hematite blueberries and silica deposits proving liquid water persisted on ancient Mars; Opportunity set driving record of 45.16 km.

majorMilestones.title: Spirit launched on Delta II
Opportunity launched on Delta II Heavy
Spirit lands in Gusev Crater
Opportunity lands in Eagle Crater (Meridiani Planum)
Spirit last communication from Troy winter haven
Opportunity last contact before global planet-encircling dust storm
NASA formally concludes Opportunity mission after 15 years

name: Mars Science Laboratory (Curiosity)
summary: Car-sized nuclear-powered rover sent to determine whether Gale Crater ever offered an environment favorable for microbial life.
outcome: Pioneered Sky Crane landing system; confirmed ancient freshwater lakes with carbon, nitrogen, oxygen, phosphorus, and sulfur.

majorMilestones.title: Atlas V launch
Touchdown via Sky Crane in Gale Crater
Yellowknife Bay drill sample confirms ancient habitable lakebed
Active exploration climbing Mount Sharp (Aeolis Mons)

name: Mars 2020 (Perseverance & Ingenuity)
summary: Astrobiology mission in Jezero Crater to search for biosignatures, collect sealed sample tubes for Earth return, and demonstrate powered aerial flight.
outcome: Perseverance cached 24+ core samples and drove 45.22 km (October 2026); Ingenuity flew 72 times across 17.0 km.

majorMilestones.title: Atlas V 541 launch
Terrain-Relative Navigation touchdown in Jezero Crater
Ingenuity achieves first powered flight on another planet
Ingenuity finishes flight mission after 72 flights
Perseverance surpasses 45.22 km total drive distance

name: Phoenix Mars Lander
summary: Stationary lander targeted to Martian arctic plains of Vastitas Borealis to verify and analyze sub-surface water ice.
outcome: Scraped trench in permafrost and directly verified water ice sublimation; discovered perchlorate salts in Martian soil.

majorMilestones.title: Delta II launch
Pulsed rocket thruster soft landing in Green Valley
Discovered subsurface white chunks that sublimated, confirming pure water ice
Solar power lost during Martian arctic winter

name: InSight
summary: Geophysical lander equipped with ultra-sensitive seismometer (SEIS) to map the crust, mantle, and molten metallic core of Mars.
outcome: Detected 1,319+ marsquakes, measured crust thickness (24–72 km), and determined core radius (~1,830 km).

majorMilestones.title: Atlas V 401 launch from Vandenberg (first West Coast planetary launch)
Touchdown in Elysium Planitia
First confirmed seismic signal detected from interior of Mars
Solar dust accumulation exhausts battery power; mission retired

name: 2001 Mars Odyssey
summary: Longest-operating spacecraft at Mars; mapped global elemental distribution and serves as primary communications relay.
outcome: Discovered vast hydrogen deposits indicating sub-surface water ice; relayed >80% of data from Spirit, Opportunity, Phoenix, and Curiosity.

majorMilestones.title: Delta II launch
Aerobraking captures spacecraft into science orbit
NASA celebrates 25th continuous year of orbital operations

name: Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (MRO)
summary: Equipped with 50 cm aperture HiRISE camera providing 30 cm/pixel imaging of the Martian surface, weather, and mineral deposits.
outcome: Scouted every landing site since 2007; identified recurring slope lineae (RSL) and relays huge volumes of data from Perseverance & Curiosity.

majorMilestones.title: Atlas V 401 launch
Mars orbit insertion and 6-month aerobraking
Celebrates 20th year in Martian orbit

name: MAVEN (Mars Atmosphere and Volatile EvolutioN)
summary: Orbiter built to measure the rate of atmospheric gas loss to space caused by solar wind stripping.
outcome: Proved that solar wind stripped away 90% of the Martian atmosphere after the planetary magnetic dynamo collapsed.

majorMilestones.title: Atlas V 401 launch
Mars orbit insertion
Announces discovery that solar storms dramatically accelerate atmospheric loss
